summary: SIEM export: audit events not normalized (inconsistent field names/shape across event types)
description:
Issue summary
Vectorgrid reports that audit events exported to Splunk HEC contain inconsistent field names and shapes depending on event type. Their SIEM correlation rules expect stable fields for actor, target, tenant, request/correlation IDs, and event taxonomy. Current inconsistency is blocking their rollout of detection rules and creating noise in dashboards.

Impact
- SIEM parsing rules break for a subset of events.
- Detection queries cannot reliably join events by actor/tenant/request.
- Customer perceives audit logging as incomplete/unreliable for compliance monitoring.

Customer expectation
- All exported events conform to the canonical v1 schema with consistent top-level fields.
- Exporter should tag schema_version and normalize legacy/variant producers into v1 shape.

Environment
- Dedicated deployment (Vectorgrid)
- Export target: Splunk HEC
- Region: us-east

Examples (customer-provided)
1) RBAC event (control plane) includes expected v1 fields:
{"event_type":"rbac.role.updated","schema_version":"1.0","event_id":"01HS...","occurred_at":"2026-01-24T18:02:11Z","tenant_id":"tnt_9f...","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"usr_4b...","actor_email":"admin@vectorgrid.com","source_ip":"203.0.113.10","request_id":"req_8c...","target_type":"role","target_id":"role_2a...","result":"success"}

2) API key event uses different names / missing fields:
{"type":"api_key_created","id":"b4d2...","timestamp":"2026-01-24T18:03:01Z","workspace":"tnt_9f...","actor":"usr_4b...","ip":"203.0.113.10","key_id":"key_77...","status":"ok"}

3) Policy change event has nested payload and inconsistent tenancy field:
{"eventType":"policy.updated","time":"2026-01-24T18:05:44Z","org_id":"tnt_9f...","actor":{"id":"svc_12...","type":"service"},"diff":{"rules_added":1},"traceId":"00-4bf9...","outcome":"SUCCESS"}

Notes
- Customer is OK with "extensions.*" for event-specific fields, but requires consistent top-level semantics.
- Customer requests guidance on whether they should normalize on their side or rely on Redwood exporter.

Requested outcome
- Confirm which schema fields are guaranteed across all sensitive actions.
- Provide patch/rollout timeline for exporter normalization + schema_version tagging.
- Provide interim workaround for Splunk field extraction rules until rollout completes.
comments: 2026-01-24 10:18 Dev Patel (Support): Opened ticket from Vectorgrid (SE escalation via #support). They sent ~200 sample events showing mixed field names. Attaching sanitized examples in description. Requesting Security Eng / Exporter owner to confirm whether this is expected prior to schema v1 rollout or a bug.

2026-01-24 11:02 Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Confirmed this is a bug/known gap. We have multiple producers emitting "legacy" shapes (pre v1) and exporter currently forwards mostly as-is. Plan is exporter-side normalization + schema_version tagging so customers can depend on stable v1 fields. Tracking in exporter PR: pr-842-add-schema-version-tagging-and-normalization. I’ll post a specific mapping list once I finish diffing the customer samples vs expected v1.

2026-01-24 12:26 Hanae Suzuki (Security Eng): Quick triage on samples: API key events appear to originate from console-backend older codepath (uses type/id/timestamp/workspace). Policy events appear to originate from policy-engine service that hasn’t adopted event_type naming convention yet. We should ensure lints reject non-registered event types going forward (ref: redwood/pr-21991).

2026-01-25 09:41 Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Proposed normalization rules (exporter):
- Map legacy keys: type|eventType -> event_type; timestamp|time -> occurred_at; id -> event_id
- Tenancy: workspace|org_id -> tenant_id
- Actor: actor string -> actor_id + actor_type=user (if prefix usr_) else service; actor object -> actor_type/actor_id
- Network: ip -> source_ip
- Correlation: traceId -> trace_id
- Outcome: status|outcome -> result (success|failure) + error_code/error_message when present
- Unknown/producer-specific fields go under extensions.*

Ask: Support confirm customer is OK with actor_email being optional (not always available for service actors).

2026-01-25 10:12 Dev Patel (Support): Confirmed with customer: actor_email optional is fine; they mostly need actor_id/actor_type/source_ip/tenant_id/event_type/occurred_at/event_id and request/trace IDs when available.

2026-01-27 16:55 Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Patch ready in exporter branch; adds schema_version=1.0 and normalization middleware. Also validates payload against schema for known event_types (best-effort: emits metric and forwards original if validation fails to avoid dropping events). Pending review from Observability (Allison) on metric naming and from SRE (Sean) on retry behavior. Linked: sources/github/audit-log-exporter/pr-842-add-schema-version-tagging-and-normalization.json

2026-01-28 09:30 Sean Gallagher (SRE): Reviewed exporter behavior. Recommend: do not block export on schema validation failure; emit counter audit_export.validation_failed and include producer_service tag (low-cardinality allow-list). Also ensure we’re not increasing payload size above Splunk HEC limits. OK to proceed if extensions payload is capped (e.g., 8KB) and truncation is explicit (extensions_truncated=true).

2026-01-29 14:07 Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Incorporated SRE feedback: extension payload cap + explicit truncation flag (extensions_truncated). Added metrics and dashboard link request for observability-pack follow-up. Preparing staged rollout to us-east Dedicated first.

2026-02-03 08:22 Dev Patel (Support): Sent customer interim workaround: update Splunk props/transforms to coalesce fields (event_type = coalesce(event_type, type, eventType), occurred_at = coalesce(occurred_at, timestamp, time), tenant_id = coalesce(tenant_id, workspace, org_id), source_ip = coalesce(source_ip, ip)). Also clarified duplicates may occur due to retry semantics; use event_id for de-dupe (linked SUP-18510).

2026-02-06 17:40 Kevin Osei (Security Eng): PR pr-842 merged. Rollout plan: enable normalization in exporter behind flag export.normalization.v1=true per environment. Targeting Vectorgrid Dedicated exporter instances in us-east on 2026-02-10 during low-traffic window.

2026-02-10 22:15 Kevin Osei (Security Eng): Flag enabled for Vectorgrid exporter. Initial metrics: validation_failed <0.3% (mostly unknown legacy eventType strings). No increased retry rate. Sending Support the list of remaining producer gaps (policy-engine + one console path) that will be fixed via producer-side adoption + lints.

2026-02-11 09:18 Dev Patel (Support): Customer confirms new events look consistent in Splunk (schema_version present; stable top-level fields). They will monitor for 48 hours before closing. Asked for written guarantee on deprecation window; pointed them to versioning/backcompat policy Confluence page.

2026-02-12 15:56 Dev Patel (Support): Customer confirmed success and unblocked correlation rules. Closing ticket. Follow-ups remain tracked internally for producer-side enforcement and reducing validation_failed to ~0.
resolution: Implemented exporter-side normalization to canonical audit schema v1 and added schema_version tagging. Rolled out normalization flag for Vectorgrid Dedicated (us-east). Provided interim Splunk coalescing workaround and guidance to de-dupe by event_id. Customer verified stable fields across event types and resumed SIEM detection rule rollout.
